text: “But why are you so long about it? You must have something on your mind—” “For heaven’s sake, let me alone, and get to bed yourself.” “Can it be that Mrs. Graham that distresses you so?” “No, no, I tell you—it’s nothing.” “I wish to goodness it mayn’t,” murmured she, with a sigh, as she returned to her own apartment, while I threw myself on the bed, feeling most undutifully disaffected towards her for having deprived me of what seemed the only shadow of a consolation that remained, and chained me to that wretched couch of thorns. Never did I endure so long, so miserable a night as that. And yet it was not wholly sleepless. Towards morning my distracting thoughts began to lose all pretensions to coherency, and shape themselves into confused and feverish dreams, and, at length, there followed an interval of unconscious slumber.
